veranderings.rede: The lesson uses the protected pair 'tekens en simptome' everywhere else; this one reversed order is the only exception and reads as a different phrase.

veranderings.voor: glo jy kry TB uit 'n beker, 'n bord of kos wat gedeel word
veranderings.na: glo jy kry TB as jy 'n beker, 'n bord of kos met iemand deel
veranderings.rede: 'TB uit 'n beker kry' with a trailing passive is wooden; an active 'as jy ... deel' is more natural and keeps the meaning.

veranderings.voor: droë hoes wat twee weke aanhou
veranderings.na: droë hoes wat twee weke lank aanhou
veranderings.rede: A duration with 'aanhou' is idiomatically 'twee weke lank aanhou', as the glossary's 'weke lank aanhou' already has it.

veranderings.blok: Ander tekens en simptome van TB
veranderings.na: Koors: die mens se liggaam is warmer
veranderings.rede: The list opens with 'sy' and 'hy' but has no antecedent under its own heading; naming the person once in the first item gives the later pronouns something to refer to.

veranderings.blok: Wat die kliniek met masels doen
veranderings.voor: masels gaan ook kliniek toe. Maar geen medisyne
veranderings.na: masels gaan ook kliniek toe, maar geen medisyne
veranderings.rede: The contrast reads more smoothly as one sentence; the AWS comma before 'maar' applies because both halves have their own subject and verb.

vlae.teks: Iemand met 'n droë hoes wat twee weke aanhou, gaan ook kliniek toe.
vlae.rede: Two sentences earlier the rule is 'twee weke of langer' with 'moet'; this sentence says only 'twee weke' and 'gaan', so the two may read as different rules. Aligning them would change content, so it is flagged, not changed.

beskerm_bedenkings.woord: TB kan gesond gemaak word / Die kliniek kan TB gesond maak
beskerm_bedenkings.rede: In Afrikaans 'gesond maak' is usually said of a person, not a disease ('n siekte word genees); the phrasing is understandable but slightly unidiomatic. Not changed, because it is protected and the forbidden list rules out the 'genees' forms.
